exposure: implementation of an obstetric hemorrhage (OBH) bundle
outcome: utilization of nonuterotonic hemorrhage interventions (uterine artery embolization, balloon tamponade)
cohort: The study included 4,275 deliveries of live births (1,944 pre-intervention and 2,331 post-intervention) at an urban tertiary care hospital.
finding: Implementation of an OBH bundle was associated with improved management, reflected in faster and increased delivery of uterotonic interventions for hemorrhage, specifically reducing mean time to oxytocin from 12.2 to 5.9 minutes.
